name: Polydactyly of an Index Finger
aliases: Preaxial Polydactyly of the Index Finger

ethnicAssociations: More common in populations of African descent

criteria.description: Presence of one or more supernumerary digits adjacent to the index finger
Radiographic evidence of duplicated phalanges or metacarpals in the index finger region
No associated syndromic anomalies or systemic malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of supernumerary digit(s) adjacent to the index finger confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be considered to rule out syndromic associations

pathognomonic.symptomName: Supernumerary digit adjacent to the index finger
searchTerms: extra finger next to index finger

pathognomonic.symptomName: Duplicated phalanges of the index finger
searchTerms: extra finger bones in index finger
index finger with extra bone segments

common.symptomName: Malformation of the metacarpal bones in the index finger
Limited range of motion in the affected finger
Soft tissue duplication around the index finger
searchTerms: extra soft tissue around index finger
additional skin or tissue on finger

occasional.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of hand grip
Associated syndactyly between index and adjacent digits
searchTerms: webbed skin between index and next finger
syndactyly of index and adjacent digit

occasional.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms in the affected finger
Localized skin irritation or ulceration over supernumerary digit
searchTerms: ulcer or sore on supernumerary digit

rare.symptomName: Associated vascular malformations in the hand
Presence of underlying bone cysts in duplicated phalanges
searchTerms: bone cysts in duplicated finger bones
fluid-filled bone lesions in extra phalanges
underlying bone cysts in extra digits

imaging: X-ray showing duplicated phalanges and/or metacarpals adjacent to the index finger
Ultrasound to assess soft tissue structures of the supernumerary digit
genetic: Mutations in GLI3 gene associated with preaxial polydactyly in some cases
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic polydactyly (e.g., Greig cephalopolysyndactyly syndrome)
other: Physical examination confirming extra digit morphology and mobility
Family history assessment for inherited patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Extra digit located on the ulnar (little finger) side of the hand
Typically less complex bone duplication compared to preaxial forms
Presence of systemic anomalies such as craniofacial abnormalities or developmental delay
Polydactyly associated with known genetic syndromes (e.g., Bardet-Biedl syndrome)

redFlags: Presence of multiple congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic polydactyly
Functional impairment of hand affecting daily activities
Signs of infection or ulceration in the supernumerary digit
